prisoner.name: Ocier S. Bratton
prisoner.description: Ocier S. Bratton helped arrange legal representation for Black sharecroppers seeking fair payment for their cotton in Phillips County, Arkansas. The son and agent of attorney Ulysses S. Bratton, he was arrested during the Elaine Massacre and spent a month in jail. His release required a guarded departure because of threats of lynching.

cases.charges: Murder accusation followed by a barratry indictment — no conviction established
cases.sentence: Arrested October 1, 1919 while obtaining legal-retainer agreements from sharecroppers near Elaine. Held in Phillips County Jail in Helena until October 31, 1919. Scipio Jones’s court petition states that a barratry indictment replaced the murder accusation on the release day and describes the judge assisting his secret departure to avoid a lynch mob. This records pretrial detention; no prison sentence or adjudicated guilt is inferred. The later disposition of the barratry indictment remains unverified.

case_research.custody_evidence: Court petition supplies both actual custody endpoints and describes continuous county-jail confinement; scholarly chronology and historical entry corroborate the month-long detention.

entries.custody_evidence: Court petition supplies both actual custody endpoints and describes continuous county-jail confinement; scholarly chronology and historical entry corroborate the month-long detention.
entries.status_research: Historical custody verified. Existing profiles, cases and photos are preserved. No unsupported vital dates, coordinates, current incarceration, institutional relation or personal support website inferred. Legal representative/agent, not assumed to be a formal union member or a member of the Elaine Twelve. FamilySearch’s sibling listing suggests expansion Simpson and1888–1951, but underlying vital records were not reviewed; dates and expanded middle name held. Neither his father’s vital dates nor his brother’s are assigned.
